# PingOne Privilege

> AI agents should consult [Docs for Agents](https://developer.pingidentity.com/build-with-ai/docs-for-agents.md)
> for guidance on navigating Ping Identity documentation.

## Privilege

- [Access protocols](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/access-protocols/index.md): PingOne Privilege supports certificate-based SSH and Remote Desktop Protocol for secure access to your resources.
- [Access request integrations](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/integrations/access-request-integrations/index.md): Connect PingOne Privilege with Jira, Microsoft Teams, ServiceNow, and Slack to manage access requests, approvals, and notifications where your teams work.
- [Accessing the PingOne Privilege admin console as an administrator](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/getting-started/accessing-admin-console.md): The admin console provides a centralized interface to configure settings, manage users, and monitor access activities.
- [Accessing the user console](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/getting-started-users/accessing-user-console.md): Users access the user console to manage and monitor privileged access across their organization.
- [Agent registry](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agent-registry.md): Add an agent in Agent Registry to register it with Agent Privilege and choose how it authenticates.
- [Agentic apps](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/index.md): Agentic apps in Agent Privilege integrate agentic applications so that AI agents can reach enterprise services securely.
- [Applications](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/request-access/applications.md): Request just-in-time access to SAML applications.
- [Atlassian](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/atlassian.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Jira, Confluence, and other Atlassian Cloud services through the MCP Catalog.
- [AWS Secrets Manager integration](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/integrations/secrets-hubs/aws-secrets-manager.md): Connect AWS Secrets Manager to PingOne Privilege as a secrets hub so users can use secrets stored in AWS secrets manager.
- [Azure Key Vault integration](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/integrations/secrets-hubs/azure-key-vault.md): Connect Azure Key Vault to PingOne Privilege as a secrets hub for users' secure credentials.
- [Brave Search](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/brave-search.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to the Brave Search API through the MCP Catalog.
- [Choosing a deployment model](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/getting-started/choosing-deployment-model.md): PingOne Privilege offers both Endpoint Controller-based and No Endpoint Controller-based deployment models to meet different organizational needs.
- [Cloud resources](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/request-access/cloud-resources.md): Request just-in-time access to Azure subscriptions.
- [Configure Agent Privilege for further use cases](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/getting-started/configure-agent-privilege.md): Configure Agent Privilege to secure AI agent traffic beyond personal agent discovery.
- [Configuring a private proxy](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/gateways/private-proxies.md): Add a private proxy to an on-premise or non-AWS cloud network to enable secure access to resources within that network.
- [Configuring a relay](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/gateways/relays.md): A relay is designed for deployment in networks that don't allow inbound connections, enabling access to resources within that private network.
- [Configuring Agent Privilege](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/index.md): Configure Agent Privilege to secure AI agent access to agentic apps, LLM providers, and Git repositories through just-in-time, least-privilege access controls.
- [Configuring AgentCore](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/agentcore.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to AWS AgentCore so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Configuring Agentforce](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/agentforce.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Salesforce Agentforce so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Configuring AI Foundry](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/ai-foundry.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Azure AI Foundry so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Configuring AI gateways](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/ai-gateways.md): The PingOne Privilege AI Gateway secures AI-agent interactions.
- [Configuring Amazon EKS access](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/configuring-kubernetes-access/aws-eks.md): The steps to configure your Amazon EKS clusters to allow access management through the PingOne Privilege platform.
- [Configuring Azure AKS access](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/configuring-kubernetes-access/azure-aks.md): The required configurations within the Azure portal to allow PingOne Privilege to discover and manage your Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters.
- [Configuring Bedrock](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/bedrock.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to AWS Bedrock so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Configuring certificate-based SSH](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/access-protocols/ssh.md): Configure your managed servers to accept SSH connections that are authenticated by short-lived certificates issued by PingOne Privilege.
- [Configuring Copilot Studio](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/copilot-studio.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Microsoft Copilot Studio so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Configuring Databricks AI](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/databricks-ai.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Databricks so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Configuring gateways for Human Privilege](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/gateways/index.md): Gateways are entry points for accessing resources on a private network, enabling secure sessions and intelligent routing.
- [Configuring GCP GKE access](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/configuring-kubernetes-access/gcp-gke.md): The required configurations within your GCP project to allow PingOne Privilege to discover and manage your GKE clusters.
- [Configuring Human Privilege](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/index.md): Learn how to set up and customize Human Privilege to suit your organization's requirements.
- [Configuring Kubernetes access](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/configuring-kubernetes-access/index.md): Configure Kubernetes access for onboarded cloud accounts to enable just-in-time access for teams running containerized workloads.
- [Configuring Lex V2](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/lex-v2.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Amazon Lex V2 so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Configuring remote desktop access](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/access-protocols/rdp.md): When you onboard a cloud account, PingOne Privilege automatically discovers all remote desktop protocol (RDP) instances.
- [Configuring Snowflake Cortex](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/snowflake-cortex.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Snowflake Cortex so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Configuring step-up authentication for sudo commands](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/multi-factor-authentication/step-up-authentication-sudo.md): Require step-up multi-factor authentication when users run sudo commands on Unix/Linux servers with just-in-time (JIT) access.
- [Configuring Vertex AI](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/vertex-ai.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Google Vertex AI so AI discovery can review its agent inventory.
- [Creating users and groups for Agent Privilege](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/getting-started/users-and-groups.md): Create the groups and users for your Agent Privilege evaluation and grant them access to PingOne Privilege.
- [Databases](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/request-access/databases.md): Request just-in-time access to MySQL and Postgres databases.
- [Delinea Secret Server integration](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/integrations/secrets-hubs/delinea-secret-server.md): Connect Delinea Secret Server to PingOne Privilege as a secrets hub for secure credential injection.
- [Deploying the Endpoint Controller on macOS with Jamf Pro](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/getting-started/deploying-controller-jamf.md): Deploy the Endpoint Controller to managed macOS computers with Jamf Pro for silent installation and automated onboarding.
- [Deploying the node sensor](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/node-sensor.md): Deploy the Privilege node sensor on Kubernetes or Docker hosts to discover agents, model servers, and MCP servers in your containers.
- [Devices](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/devices.md): Every registered device is associated with a user.
- [Discover agents running on a workstation](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/getting-started/discover-agents.md): Turn on personal agent discovery and review the first agents found on your onboarded workstation.
- [Discover and manage NHI agents](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/use-cases/nhi-agents.md): AI Discovery for NHI agents finds non-human identity agents operating in your environment and helps you govern them.
- [Discover and manage personal agents](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/use-cases/personal-agents.md): AI discovery finds the AI agents operating in your environment, whether they run on user devices, in workloads, or under non-human identities.
- [Discover and manage workload agents](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/use-cases/workload-agents.md): AI discovery finds the workload agents operating in your environment, whether they run on user devices, in workloads, or under non-human identities.
- [Elasticsearch](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/elasticsearch.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Elasticsearch clusters and indices through the MCP Catalog.
- [GCP Secrets Manager integration](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/integrations/secrets-hubs/gcp-secrets-manager.md): Connect GCP Secrets Manager to PingOne Privilege as a secrets hub for secure credential injection.
- [Getting started with Agent Privilege](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/getting-started/index.md): Get started with Agent Privilege to secure personal AI agents in an Endpoint Controller-based deployment.
- [Getting started with Human Privilege](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/getting-started.md): Get started with Human Privilege: sign on to the console, then jump to the use cases for administrators or users.
- [Git Server](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/git-server.md): A Git Server is a system used to host and manage Git repositories. Agent Privilege secures Git Server applications so that AI agent commits are attributable.
- [GitHub](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/github.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to GitHub repositories, issues, and pull requests through the MCP Catalog.
- [Grafana](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/grafana.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Grafana dashboards and data sources through the MCP Catalog.
- [Installing the Endpoint Controller and accessing the admin console](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/getting-started/onboarding-endpoint-controller.md): Install the Endpoint Controller with an onboarding link, approve the macOS system extensions, and access the PingOne Privilege admin console.
- [Integrations](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/integrations/index.md): Integrate PingOne Privilege with collaboration services and external secrets hubs to manage privileged access where your teams work
- [Jira integration](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/integrations/access-request-integrations/jira.md): The Jira integration automatically creates and updates Jira issues to track just-in-time access requests.
- [Key concepts](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/getting-started/key-concepts.md): Understand the foundational concepts of PingOne Privilege.
- [Kubernetes clusters](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/request-access/kubernetes-clusters.md): Users can request just-in-time access at the cluster, namespace, or pod level.
- [Managing access requests](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/access-management/access-requests.md): An organization administrator can perform the following actions on a user's just-in-time access requests.
- [Managing access requests](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/activity/access-request-approval-logs.md): Review, approve, and manage the lifecycle of user access requests for resources.
- [Managing access requests](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/access-request-management/access-requests.md): Create, view, and manage your just-in-time access requests in the user portal.
- [Managing activity logs](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/activity/activity-logs.md): Gain full visibility into user activity and system events.
- [Managing cloud resources](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/access-management/cloud-accounts.md): When you register a cloud account the Endpoint Controller periodically scans the account to discover its resources.
- [Managing devices](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/directory-management/devices.md): Every registered device is uniquely associated with a single user, and each user can have one or more registered devices.
- [Managing groups](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/directory-management/groups.md): Groups are collections of users that can be used to assign access policies efficiently.
- [Managing passwordless access](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/access-management/passwordless-access.md): This feature eliminates the need for users to manage or directly handle static credentials, such as passwords or SSH keys, for the target systems.
- [Managing policies](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/access-management/policies.md): Policies automatically grant permissions to users or groups based on predefined criteria.
- [Managing service accounts](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/directory-management/service-accounts.md): Service accounts in PingOne Privilege provide secure, just-in-time credentials for programmatic access by applications, scripts, and automation tools.
- [Managing session logs](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/activity/session-logs.md): If session logging is enabled for your tenant, PingOne Privilege records all SSH and database sessions.
- [Managing users](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/directory-management/users.md): This topic describes how users and roles are managed for PingOne Privilege.
- [MCP Aggregate](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/mcp-aggregate.md): An MCP Aggregate application aggregates multiple MCP servers behind a single application in Agent Privilege.
- [MCP Server](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/mcp-server.md): An MCP Server application in Agent Privilege fronts a backend MCP server so that AI agents get just-in-time, least-privilege access with full session visibility.
- [Microsoft Teams](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/integrations/access-request-integrations/microsoft-teams.md): The PingOne Privilege Microsoft Teams integration allows your teams to receive notifications of access requests or approvals.
- [MongoDB](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/mongodb.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to MongoDB databases through the MCP Catalog.
- [Multi-factor authentication](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/multi-factor-authentication/index.md): Require multi-factor authentication when users connect the PingOne Privilege app and when they run privileged commands.
- [Onboarding Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/cloud-accounts/aws.md): When you add an AWS account to PingOne Privilege, its resources are discovered automatically and can be managed for just-in-time (JIT) developer access.
- [Onboarding Azure accounts](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/cloud-accounts/azure.md): When an Azure subscription is added to PingOne Privilege, its resources are automatically discovered and can be managed for just-in-time developer access.
- [Onboarding cloud accounts](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/cloud-accounts/index.md): Enable passwordless, just-in-time access to resources across various cloud infrastructures.
- [Onboarding GCP accounts](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/configuration/cloud-accounts/gcp.md): Onboard a GCP organization, folder, or project to manage its resources in PingOne Privilege with Just-In-Time (JIT) access.
- [Onboarding users](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/getting-started/onboarding-users.md): This topic describes how organization administrators can onboard users to the PingOne Privilege user console.
- [OpenAPI MCP](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/openapi-mcp.md): An OpenAPI MCP application exposes APIs described by OpenAPI specifications to AI agents over MCP in Agent Privilege.
- [OpenSearch](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/opensearch.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to OpenSearch clusters and indices through the MCP Catalog.

- [Redis](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/redis.md): Connect PingOne Privilege to Redis data stores through the MCP Catalog.
- [Registering non-human identities](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/non-human-identities.md): Register the non-human identities that authenticate to Agent Privilege with signed tokens instead of stored credentials.
- [Remote Agent](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/agentic-apps/remote-agent.md): A Remote Agent application registers an agent that connects to PingOne Privilege from outside your network.
- [Remote desktop](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/request-access/remote-desktop.md): Request just-in-time access to Remote Desktop.
- [Request access to cloud virtual servers](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/request-access/servers.md): Request just-in-time access to Amazon Web Services (AWS) EC2, Google Compute, and Azure virtual servers.
- [Requesting access to AWS IAM roles](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/request-access/aws-role-cli.md): Request just-in-time access to AWS identity and access management roles.

- [Use cases for administrators](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/admin-use-cases/index.md): What administrators can do in Human Privilege: manage the directory, control access to resources, and monitor activity.
- [Use cases for users](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/user-use-cases/index.md): What users can do in Human Privilege: request access to resources, manage requests, manage devices, and view activity.

- [What is Agent Privilege?](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/what-is-agent-privilege.md): Agent Privilege is PingOne Privilege's identity and security control plane for AI agents.
- [What is Human Privilege?](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/human-privilege/what-is-human-privilege.md): Human Privilege secures human access to critical resources with modern privileged access management.
- [What is PingOne Privilege?](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/getting-started/introduction.md): PingOne Privilege provides secure, passwordless, just-in-time access to cloud infrastructure for people, and secures the AI agents acting on their behalf.
- [Workload agent applications](https://docs.pingidentity.com/privilege/agent-privilege/configuration/workload-agent-apps/index.md): Add the workload agent applications that connect Agent Privilege AI discovery to your cloud platforms.
